test_name: decbench round-2 triage, NOVEL pool (rodata-phantom-store, re-triage)
inspiration: docs/decbench/triage/rodata-phantom-store.md (symptom); mechanism re-derived by instrumenting SplitDatatype::test_copy_constraints -- the filed is_return_copy() predicate is refuted
gating_rationale: Emitting a store the program never performs is wrong output, not a judgment call, so CLAUDE.md's flag rule exempts it; there is no honest use_when prose for a knob that re-enables a store into read-only memory. A bisector already has `option togglerule splitcopy off` (splitcopy is the rule's registered name in the action pool, infra/universalaction.rs:558). Recorded as DIV-55 in docs/history.md because the added test is a divergence from upstream subflow.cc:2390 -- not a Convergence: nothing was restored, and the precondition it guards against is created by another kuna divergence (stackguard, DIV-14).

gates.make test-stages: 375/375 PARITY OK (baseline re-recorded: purely additive, 369 -> 375 keys, no existing assertion moved)
gates.kuna catalog --check: catalog OK (no option added; phases.toml, p0_knowledge/options.rs, the catalog counts and docs/options.md are untouched)

stage_test.passes: two-pass: pass 1 default (the fix), pass 2 `option togglerule splitcopy off` (the reference rendering, no split at all)
stage_test.note: real iproute2 `ip` bytes: __get_hz at its real VMA 0x6cbf0 (433 bytes verbatim, plus one synthetic 0xc3 so the fall-through of the final `call __stack_chk_fail` terminates -- the PLT stub is outside the chunk so the engine cannot know it does not return), plus the 32-byte read-only literal at 0x92e50. `map addr r0x92e50 char s_92e50[32]` stands in for the strings analysis pass, which does not run on a bytechunk image.

mechanism_note: Instrumented `test_copy_constraints` on the witness function. The two ops that produce all 16 phantom statements are `0x00020fb0:119b` and `:119c`: rc=false, input at a unique (0x1000044a / 0x10000452, not addr-tied), output addr-tied at ram:0x822f0 / ram:0x822f8 with ro=true and persist=true. The genuine heritage return-copies at the same addresses (`:b56`, `:b97`) carry rc=true and are already declined by upstream's same-address gate. The real copy site (`0x00021160:b1f`, `:b20`) copies FROM the literal INTO the stack with ro=false on the output, and is still split after the fix.

regression_sweep.method: whole-binary `kuna decompile-all --json` with a before/after release build pair of this worktree, diffed per function address
regression_sweep.no_real_store_lost: after the fix every surviving assignment whose LHS is an address-named global lands in a writable (WA) section -- bash 22 (.data/.bss), tar 6 (.bss), coreutils sort 4 (.data), dpkg 1 (.data), sshd 1 (.bss) -- and every one of those counts is identical before and after

speed_method: interleaved A/B on two release builds of this worktree (base vs patched), medians of N pairs; `scripts.pipeline.timeit` is inapplicable -- it measures an option flip and this fix has no option
speed_note: There is no mechanism for a cost: the fix adds one varnode-flag test per COPY that RuleSplitCopy already considers, and a declined split does strictly less work than a taken one. The measurements say the same, with the honest caveat that the box runs concurrent agents: a byte-identical control function moved -12.18% and -20.23% across two runs, and a byte-identical whole binary (coreutils sort) moved +9.17% and +1.42%, so anything inside roughly +/-10% here is load, not signal. On the highest-pair-count run of every changed target the delta is -1.08%, +0.41% and -10.69%.
ged_note: GED-neutral by construction: the fix deletes statements inside one basic block on one return path and creates/destroys no block and no edge, so the graph-edit-distance metric cannot see it. This case is ranked by correctness (a store the program never performs), not by GED.

decisions.question: Which predicate declines the split?
decisions.verdict: the COPY's OUTPUT varnode is_read_only(), NOT is_return_copy()
decisions.rationale: Instrumentation (see mechanism_note) shows is_return_copy() is dead on this path: the flag does not survive CloneBlockOps::build_op_clone, which is the op that produces the phantom, and the un-cloned form is already declined by upstream's same-address gate. Read-only-ness of the destination is the property that survives the clone AND the property that actually makes the statement wrong.

decisions.question: Ship behind a --option, or ungated?
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md gates features -- 'behavior that is a judgment call, not universally better' -- and exempts 'a strict bug fix that only corrects wrong output'. A store into a section the loader reports as non-writable is not a judgment call. The 15,386-function sweep shows the blast radius is exactly the 3 phantom functions and that no store into a writable global is touched. Precedent: DIV-46, DIV-49, DIV-50, DIV-52 and the funcptralign/subright Convergences all change emitted C ungated; a bisection switch already exists (`option togglerule splitcopy off`).

decisions.question: DIV row or Convergences entry in docs/history.md?
decisions.rationale: docs/history.md defines a Convergence as 'a port defect whose fix moves kuna back onto upstream's default'. Nothing was restored here: the test does not exist in upstream subflow.cc:2390, and the CFG shape that exposes the hole is produced by kuna's own stackguard divergence (DIV-14), so upstream cannot reach the case at all. That makes it an intentional change to default behaviour vs upstream, which is exactly what the DIV registry records.

decisions.question: Also fix the clone fidelity in CloneBlockOps::build_op_clone (carry return_copy across the clone)?
decisions.rationale: That mask is a verbatim transcription of upstream funcdata_block.cc:982-988 (its comment already documents one faithful upstream quirk), so changing it is a second, wider divergence affecting every node-split, not just this one. One fix, one PR. The read-only output test closes the emitted-C bug on its own, corpus-wide.
